raised.claim: Guard 3 degrades an unproven `not_on_untappd` verdict to `matcher_bug` and pushes it into `plan.quiet`, but the job counts every quiet verdict that is not `not_on_untappd` as `wontfix`, so those rows are reported as `wontfix` in the daily digest instead of their real class.
raised.why_it_breaks: Input: a `not_on_untappd` verdict with no probe evidence (probes empty). `planTriageActions` runs guard 3 and pushes `{...verdict, review_class: 'matcher_bug', ...}` into `quiet`. The job later executes the unchanged loop `for (const v of plan.quiet) { review(v, null); if (v.review_class === 'not_on_untappd') outcome.notOnUntappd++; else outcome.wontfix++; }`. Because the degraded verdict is now `matcher_bug`, `outcome.notOnUntappd` is NOT incremented and `outcome.wontfix` IS incremented. `buildTriageLine` then prints "N wontfix" for rows that were actually classified `matcher_bug` (and were originally `not_on_untappd`), misreporting the daily triage result and hiding the absence-verdict count.

raised.quote:
const body = `${issue.body}\n\n${renderScopeBlock(issue.scope)}`;
        const number = await github.createIssue({ title: issue.title, body, labels: issue.labels });
raised.claim: The job appends the rendered scope block after the model's `issue.body`, but `parseScopeBlock` takes the FIRST ```triage-scope match, so any fence inside the model-authored body is parsed on the next run instead of the block we appended.
raised.why_it_breaks:
Input: the LLM returns a new_issue whose free-text `body` contains a ```triage-scope fence (e.g. it echoes the format or pastes an example) earlier in the body. The job creates the issue with `body = modelBody + "

" + renderScopeBlock(issue.scope)`. On the next run `parseScopeBlock(i.body)` (regex `/```triage-scope\s*
([\s\S]*?)
?```/` in triage-scope.ts, first-match) matches the model's fence, not ours, and returns that scope. Guard 2 then evaluates every row against the wrong scope: legitimate batch rows are refused with `scope_violation` (skipped, review_class stays NULL) and unrelated rows can be accepted. This is the same silent-wrong-scope failure the diff fixed for `contains` values but did not fix for the issue body.

raised.claim: `guardHits` is only logged inside `if (covered < orphans.length)`, but `covered` counts pre-guard verdicts, so in the normal case (the model returns a verdict for every orphan) the shortfall warning — and therefore all guard visibility — is never emitted.
raised.why_it_breaks: `covered` is computed from `analysis.verdicts` (before any guard runs), and the prompt tells the model to "Classify EVERY orphan", so normally every batch beer_id has a verdict and `covered === orphans.length`. The `if (covered < orphans.length)` condition is therefore false and the `log.warn({ ..., guardHits: plan.guardHits })` never runs, even when guards skipped many verdicts (e.g. `scope_violation: 6`). The PR's stated purpose — making guard hits visible in one line — is unreachable in the normal full-coverage case; only a model that omits some orphans triggers it.

raised.claim: The tool schema allows a string `value` for any scope term, but `ScopeTermSchema` requires `z.number()` for numeric columns, so a model sending `value: "0"` makes the whole analysis fail to parse and closes the day with an error instead of being handled by a guard.
raised.why_it_breaks: `ANALYSIS_TOOL_SCHEMA` declares `value: { type: ['string', 'number', 'null'] }` for every where-term (required by strict tool use), so a model may legally submit `{col:'candidates_count', op:'=', value:'0'}` (a string). `ScopeTermSchema`'s numeric variant uses `value: z.number()`, which rejects a string. `AnalysisSchema.safeParse` then fails on the whole `where` array, `llm.analyze` throws a ZodError, and the job catch treats it as non-transient (`isTransient` false) and calls `finish({ ...outcome, error, attempt: null })`, closing the Warsaw day with an error and triaging nothing.
